subproblem.title: Limits of bounded weighted point sums in a compact set are finite integer point sums
subproblem.statement: Let P, C ∈ ℕ and let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. Let N : ℕ → ℕ, w : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ and x : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ^P satisfy x_{j,l} ∈ K and w_{j,l} ≠ 0 whenever l < N_j, and Σ_{l<N_j} |w_{j,l}| ≤ C for every j. Let ι be a type, and for k ∈ ι let g_k : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous and t_k ∈ ℝ, such that Σ_{l<N_j} w_{j,l} g_k(x_{j,l}) → t_k as j → ∞ for every k. Then there are M ∈ ℕ, v : ℕ → ℤ and y : ℕ → ℝ^P with y_l ∈ K for l < M and t_k = Σ_{l<M} v_l g_k(y_l) for every k ∈ ι.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)) (C : ℕ) (N : ℕ → ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ) (x : ℕ → ℕ → Euclid P) (ι : Type) (g : ι → Euclid P → ℝ) (t : ι → ℝ), IsCompact K → (∀ j l, l < N j → x j l ∈ K) → (∀ j l, l < N j → w j l ≠ 0) → (∀ j, (∑ l ∈ Finset.range (N j), (w j l).natAbs) ≤ C) → (∀ k, Continuous (g k)) → (∀ k, Tendsto (fun j => ∑ l ∈ Finset.range (N j), (w j l : ℝ) * g k (x j l)) atTop (𝓝 (t k))) → ∃ (M : ℕ) (v : ℕ → ℤ) (y : ℕ → Euclid P), (∀ l < M, y l ∈ K) ∧ ∀ k, t k = ∑ l ∈ Finset.range M, (v l : ℝ) * g k (y l)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 4–5: N_j and the signs take finitely many values and B̄_{2r}(x₀)^N is compact, so a subsequence has constant count, constant signs and convergent points, and the limit is identified by continuity. Here integer weights w_{j,l} replace points listed |w_{j,l}| times with sign ±1; the bounds of step 1 give the same finiteness. Simon's printed proof of Ch. 6, 8.2 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 2322–2323) only says that "the theorem is trivial in case n = 0", so this argument is extracted and specialized from the parent-supplied proof (Part III, CL(0)).

1. Bounds. For l < N_j, w_{j,l} ≠ 0 gives |w_{j,l}| ≥ 1 (Int.natAbs_pos), so N_j = Σ_{l<N_j} 1 ≤ Σ_{l<N_j} |w_{j,l}| ≤ C. Also |w_{j,l}| ≤ Σ_{l'<N_j} |w_{j,l'}| ≤ C for l < N_j (Finset.single_le_sum), i.e. −C ≤ w_{j,l} ≤ C.
2. Constant combinatorial type. Put δ_j := (N_j, u_j) ∈ ℕ × ℤ^{Fin C}, where u_j(l) := w_{j,l} if l < N_j and u_j(l) := 0 otherwise (l ranging over Fin C). By step 1, every δ_j lies in the finite set S := {0, …, C} × {−C, …, C}^{Fin C}. Since ℕ is infinite and S is finite, some d = (N₀, u₀) ∈ S has an infinite fibre (Mathlib Finite.exists_infinite_fiber), i.e. δ_j = d frequently along atTop (Nat.frequently_atTop_iff_infinite). Hence there is a strictly increasing φ₁ : ℕ → ℕ with δ_{φ₁(j)} = d for all j (extraction_of_frequently_atTop). Consequently N_{φ₁(j)} = N₀ ≤ C and w_{φ₁(j),l} = u₀(l) for all j and all l < N₀.
3. Convergent points. X_j := (x_{φ₁(j),l})_{l<N₀} ∈ (ℝ^P)^{Fin N₀} lies in K^{Fin N₀} because N_{φ₁(j)} = N₀, and K^{Fin N₀} is compact (Mathlib isCompact_univ_pi). As (ℝ^P)^{Fin N₀} is a metric space, there are a ∈ K^{Fin N₀} and a strictly increasing φ₂ with X_{φ₂(j)} → a (Mathlib IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). Put ψ := φ₁ ∘ φ₂; it is strictly increasing, so ψ(j) → ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop).
4. Identification of the limit. Fix k ∈ ι. By step 2 and reindexing (Finset.sum_range), for every j,
Σ_{l<N_{ψ(j)}} w_{ψ(j),l} g_k(x_{ψ(j),l}) = Σ_{l<N₀} u₀(l) g_k(X_{φ₂(j)}(l)).
(i) The left side tends to t_k: it is the hypothesis' convergent sequence composed with ψ → ∞ (Tendsto.comp).
(ii) The right side tends to Σ_{l<N₀} u₀(l) g_k(a_l): each coordinate X_{φ₂(j)}(l) → a_l (continuity of evaluation, continuous_apply), g_k is continuous, and finite sums and constant multiples of convergent sequences converge (tendsto_finsetSum, Tendsto.const_mul).
By uniqueness of limits in ℝ (tendsto_nhds_unique), t_k = Σ_{l<N₀} u₀(l) g_k(a_l).
5. Put M := N₀; v_l := u₀(l) for l < C and v_l := 0 for l ≥ C (so v_l = u₀(l) for l < N₀ ≤ C); y_l := a_l for l < N₀ and y_l := 0 for l ≥ N₀. Then y_l ∈ K for l < M because a ∈ K^{Fin N₀}, and by step 4 (and Finset.sum_range) t_k = Σ_{l<M} v_l g_k(y_l) for every k ∈ ι. ∎

the sums along the subsequence tend to t_k and, by continuity of g_k, to Σ u₀(l) g_k(a_l); uniqueness of limits
